newsitem.title: UK: Reuters, others down on tax ruling.
newsitem.headline: Reuters, others down on tax ruling.

text.p: Shares in Reuters Holdings Plc and other companies planning or likely to make share buybacks or special dividend payments dropped on Tuesday after the UK Treasury ruled out tax credits for such arrangements.
Reuters, which announced plans for a 613 million bonus share issue in September, was down 23p at 753-1/2 by 0750 GMT.
Other companies in a strong cash position were also lower, with Great Universal Stores Plc down 17-1/2p at 609 and Barclays Plc down 21p at 953-1/2.

As bank and utility stocks were seen as among the biggest casualties of the UK Treasury ruling, National Westminster Bank Plc was down 23-1/2p at 688-1/2, United Utilities Plc was down 18p at 558-1/2, Severn Trent Plc was down 20p at 586 and PowerGen Plc was down 20-1/2p at 469.
In a statement, Chancellor Kenneth Clarke said shareholders who previously would have been able to claim tax credits on share buybacks or special dividend payouts would no longer be able to do so.

Dealers said the move would reduce the value to tax-exempt investment funds of special buybacks and could make companies less keen to use such schemes to utilise cash surpluses, though special payouts could still continue.
"A share buyback or special dividend might now be worth somewhat less," said one head of equity sales, "but that doesn't mean that it isn't going to happen."
"It was perhaps a little too much of a gravy train to continue. I don't think anyone should be too surprised that this happened," the head of equity sales said.
Shares later rebounded from their initial mark-down, leaving Reuters down just 14p at 763 by 0815 GMT and GUS down 6p at 620-1/2.
A spokesman for Reuters declined to comment on the Treasury announcement.
